ann_89.text: Calls to customer service clearly add to the predicted chance from about 3 calls upwards: going from 0 to 4 calls moves a typical customer from about 1% to about 14%.
Daytime minutes clearly add to it only once they rise above about 198 (from 0 to 271 minutes, about 1% to 9%), and more so if evening minutes are above 201 (about 1% to 7%, against 1% to 2%).
For a typical customer, more daytime, evening and night-time minutes, going from 0 to 3 calls and a voice-mail plan each change it only slightly.

This part acts on 1795 of 4000 customers (453 of them left), and for a typical one (in New Jersey, with two customer-service calls and about 206 daytime minutes) it raises the predicted chance only slightly, from about 2% to about 3%.
A daytime charge above about $40.05 for customers without a voice-mail plan, and being in Louisiana or South Dakota, change it only slightly (on the training data only).

ann_90.text: This part acts on 380 of 4000 customers, and 161 of them left.
For a typical customer it acts on (in Illinois, with an international plan), it clearly raises the predicted chance from about 1% to about 24%.
An international plan clearly raises it from about 1% to about 15% for a typical customer, and even more so for customers in Iowa (about 1% to 31%).
For the customer it acts on, being in Iowa raises it from about 24% to about 38%, and being in Missouri raises it only slightly (on the training data only).

ann_91.text: This part acts on 3988 of 4000 customers (566 of them left), and for a typical one it lowers the predicted chance only slightly, from about 2% to about 1% (on the training data only).
Daytime and evening charges, night-time minutes and international minutes change it only slightly, and so does being in Pennsylvania, Tennessee or Indiana (on the training data only).

ann_92.text: Through this part, being in Washington raises the predicted chance for a typical customer only slightly, from about 1% to about 5%, and Louisiana, New Jersey, South Dakota, Kentucky, Colorado, Ohio and Vermont change it only slightly (on the training data only).
More evening calls lower it only slightly (on the training data only).

ann_93.text: Area code 510 lowers the predicted chance only slightly (on the training data only).
One small part barely changes the predictions.

ann_94.text: A longer account raises the predicted chance only slightly, from an account length of about 60 upwards (on the training data only).
This part acts on 3341 of 4000 customers, and 484 of them left.

ann_95.text: In this straight-line part, voice-mail messages and plan, international charge, calls and minutes, evening and night-time minutes, account length and the state each change the predicted chance only slightly (on the training data only).

ann_96.text: Across the whole model, an international plan clearly raises the predicted chance for a typical customer from about 1% to about 15%.
Going from 0 to 3 customer-service calls (about 1% to 3%), more daytime minutes (about 1% to 3%) and a voice-mail plan each change it only slightly.

Being in Washington (about 5%) or another state, voice-mail messages, account length, international charge, calls and minutes, evening charge and calls, and area code 510 each change it only slightly (on the training data only).
